chapter: Big bands, small groups and studio work
title: Make Mine Music and replacing Goodman at the Paramount

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: So let's see, we talked a bit already about Carmen Jones. Anything else you'd like to mention about that?
Carmen Jones, no. Only of course during that time I was doing the two shows which I mentioned before and .....
It says here you worked with Benny Goodman for a film called Make Mine Music in June of '44. What do you recall about that?

Well nothing, only it was a good session, you know, and it was Charlie Shavers I think was on it, I forget now. It was a very good session and that's all it was, we just did that and that was it. It was like a recording date. It was a good little thing, though, Make Mine Music, good tunes, it sounded good; we heard the playbacks.
There in New York over on the east side in one of those studios, I forget now.
So you were after that doubled in Carmen Jones and in Seven Lively Arts as you mentioned earlier. It says briefly with Benny Goodman February to March '46.
That's right. See, I did eight weeks with him at the Paramount Theatre.
Well Louie Bellson replaced me with Benny Goodman. He had just been discharged from the army, so when he was discharged, he replaced me and I went back to my studio work and my drum school.
